modules.title: Supporting Mobile Software
lessons: 20B Troubleshoot Mobile OS and App Software
20C Troubleshoot Mobile OS and App Security

questions.question: Which item belongs in the description/progress information of a support ticket?
options: The issue description and progress notes
questions.explanation: The objectives identify issue description, progress notes, and issue resolution as clear, concise ticket communication.

questions.question: Which system is used to track hardware, software, licensing, and asset lifecycle information?
questions.explanation: The Student Guide describes a CMDB as a place to track assets and can include software, licensing, and lifecycle information.

questions.question: A customer is upset and raising their voice. Which response matches the documented professional approach?
options: Argue until the customer accepts the technician's view
Assume the customer caused the problem
Remain calm, actively listen, and focus on positive actions
questions.explanation: The guide says not to argue or dismiss the issue, to avoid judgment, and to actively listen while moving toward resolution.

questions.question: Which communication practice is specifically recommended when technical jargon may confuse a customer?
options: Only communicate through undocumented verbal instructions
Use as many acronyms as possible
Use proper language and avoid jargon, acronyms, and slang when applicable
questions.explanation: The Core 2 objectives explicitly call for proper language and avoiding jargon, acronyms, and slang when applicable.

questions.question: Which operating system is categorized as a mobile OS in the Core 2 objectives?
questions.explanation: The objectives list iPadOS, iOS, and Android under mobile operating systems.

questions.question: Which filesystem is listed in the Core 2 objectives as an Apple filesystem?
questions.explanation: Apple File System (APFS) is explicitly listed among the filesystem types in the objectives.

questions.question: A user says the laptop should enter a power-saving state when the lid is closed. Which Windows setting category should be checked?
questions.explanation: The Windows settings objectives include Power Options, including what happens when closing the lid.

questions.question: Which Windows setting controls whether hidden files are displayed in File Explorer?
questions.explanation: The objectives list File Explorer Options with View hidden files and Hide extensions.

questions.question: Which Windows feature controls prompts or administrator credentials when administrative settings are changed?
questions.explanation: The Student Guide describes UAC as a mechanism to prevent unauthorized use of administrator privileges.

questions.question: Which Windows settings area is used to configure date, time zone, region, keyboard input, and language?
questions.explanation: The Student Guide describes Time and Language settings as covering date/time, time zone, region, keyboard input, and languages.

questions.question: An application requires 64-bit support and a specific amount of RAM and storage. What should the technician check first?
questions.explanation: The objectives require consideration of 32-bit/64-bit requirements, RAM, CPU, VRAM, storage, and OS compatibility.

questions.question: Which cloud productivity area in the objectives includes synchronization of folders?
questions.explanation: The cloud-based productivity objective explicitly includes storage with sync/folder settings.

questions.question: Which Windows console is intended for viewing and managing system event logs?
questions.explanation: Event Viewer is the MMC snap-in for viewing and managing Windows logs.

questions.question: Which MMC snap-in is used to manage disks and partitions?
questions.explanation: Disk Management is explicitly listed for managing disks and partitions in the Windows toolset.

questions.question: Which command displays the current user's username and domain/computer information?
questions.explanation: The Student Guide describes whoami as displaying the current user's username and domain information.

questions.question: Which command is used to display Windows version information?
questions.explanation: The guide identifies winver as the command that provides Windows version information.

questions.question: A technician needs to view IP addressing information on a Windows client. Which command is appropriate?
questions.explanation: The Core 2 objectives list ipconfig under Windows network command-line tools.

questions.question: Which Windows network configuration concept determines whether an address is manually assigned or obtained dynamically?
questions.explanation: The networking objectives explicitly include static vs. dynamic client network configuration.

questions.question: A Windows client cannot resolve a domain name. Which configuration should be checked as part of client network settings?
questions.explanation: DNS settings are explicitly listed under Windows client network configuration.

questions.question: Which protocol connects to a command interpreter and uses TCP port 22 by default?
questions.explanation: The Student Guide states that SSH is a remote access protocol to a command interpreter and uses TCP port 22 by default.

questions.question: Which remote access method is described as Microsoft's implementation of WS-Management?
questions.explanation: The guide identifies WinRM as Microsoft's implementation of the WS-Management protocol.

questions.question: Which Windows tool provides an inventory of hardware/software components, firmware and OS versions, driver locations, environment variables, and network status?
questions.explanation: The Student Guide describes msinfo32.exe as generating a comprehensive system hardware/software report.

questions.question: Which Windows log records audit data for the system?
questions.explanation: The guide lists Security Log as holding audit data for the system.

questions.question: Which symptom is explicitly listed as a common Windows OS issue?
questions.explanation: BSOD is explicitly listed under common Windows OS issues in the Core 2 objectives.

questions.question: Which security principle gives users only the access required to perform their tasks?
questions.explanation: The security objectives explicitly list the principle of least privilege as a logical security control.

questions.question: Which technology allows a user to authenticate once and access multiple supported services?
questions.explanation: SSO is listed as a logical security technology in the objectives.

questions.question: Which Windows feature encrypts a drive to protect data at rest?
questions.explanation: BitLocker is explicitly listed among Windows security settings and is used for drive encryption.

questions.question: Which Windows security feature prompts for confirmation or administrator credentials when an administrative action requires elevation?
questions.explanation: The Student Guide describes UAC as preventing unauthorized use of administrator privileges by requiring confirmation or credentials at its default level.

questions.question: Which two permission layers are specifically compared when securing Windows shared resources?
questions.explanation: The objectives explicitly include NTFS vs. share permissions.

questions.question: Which Active Directory action applies centralized configuration settings to users or computers?
questions.explanation: The Windows security objectives include applying Group Policy in Active Directory.

questions.question: Which Windows edition is listed in the objectives for both Windows 10 and Windows 11?
questions.explanation: Home is listed under both Windows 10 and Windows 11 editions.

questions.question: Which Windows feature is listed as an edition difference?
questions.explanation: The objectives list BitLocker among Windows edition feature differences.

questions.question: Which installation type replaces the existing OS installation rather than updating it in place?
questions.explanation: A clean install is explicitly contrasted with an upgrade/in-place upgrade in the installation objectives.

questions.question: Which partitioning scheme is abbreviated GPT?
questions.explanation: GPT stands for GUID Partition Table in the objectives.

questions.question: Before an OS upgrade, which consideration is explicitly recommended?
options: Back up files and user preferences
questions.explanation: The objectives explicitly include backing up files and user preferences before an upgrade.

questions.question: Which deployment method aims to configure systems with minimal hands-on interaction?
questions.explanation: Zero-touch deployment is one of the installation/deployment types listed in the objectives.

questions.question: Which Linux command lists directory contents?
questions.explanation: The Linux objectives list ls under file management.

questions.question: Which Linux command changes file permissions?
questions.explanation: The objectives list chmod under Linux file management.

questions.question: Which Linux command is described as a powerful tool for network configuration and management and can display routes?
questions.explanation: The Student Guide describes ip as a network configuration/management tool and gives ip route show as an example.

questions.question: Which Linux package manager is listed for Debian-family systems?
questions.explanation: The objectives list apt and dnf as Linux package-management tools.

questions.question: Which macOS feature provides backups and can restore the entire system or specific files?
questions.explanation: The Student Guide describes Time Machine as a backup and restoration feature.

questions.question: Which macOS utility can be used to reformat and repair the system disk?
questions.explanation: Disk Utility is explicitly listed among macOS features and tools.

questions.question: A malicious email targets a senior executive with a tailored message. Which social engineering category best matches the objectives?
questions.explanation: Whaling is listed as a phishing-related social engineering attack in the objectives.

questions.question: Which attack overwhelms a service with traffic from multiple distributed sources?
questions.explanation: DDoS is explicitly listed as a threat; the distributed nature distinguishes it from a basic DoS attack.

questions.question: Which wireless security option is newer than WPA2 in the objectives?
questions.explanation: The objectives list WPA2 and WPA3 as wireless security protocols, with WPA3 being the newer protocol in that pair.

questions.question: Which authentication service is listed for wireless security authentication?
questions.explanation: RADIUS is explicitly listed under authentication methods.

questions.question: Which router setting helps prevent unauthorized administrative access by replacing vendor defaults?
questions.explanation: Changing default passwords is explicitly listed as a SOHO router security setting.

questions.question: Which wireless setting can be used to separate visitors from the main network?
questions.explanation: Configuring guest access is explicitly listed under wireless-specific router security settings.

questions.question: Which account practice is explicitly listed as a workstation hardening measure?
questions.explanation: Failed-attempt lockout is listed under account management hardening techniques.

questions.question: Which authentication method is included in the Windows login options?
questions.explanation: The Windows security objectives include passwordless/Windows Hello among login options.

questions.question: Which practice protects data if a storage device is lost or stolen?
questions.explanation: Data-at-rest encryption is explicitly listed as a workstation security/hardening measure.

questions.question: Which setting should be disabled when it is not needed because it can automatically launch content from removable media?
questions.explanation: The workstation-hardening objectives explicitly include disabling AutoRun.

questions.question: Which browser feature helps prevent unwanted pop-up windows?
questions.explanation: The browser-security objectives explicitly list a pop-up blocker.

questions.question: A user sees repeated fake antivirus warnings in the browser. Which category of symptom is this?
questions.explanation: The objectives list false alerts regarding antivirus protection and browser-related symptoms such as pop-ups and certificate warnings.

questions.question: Which mobile security measure protects the device if someone gains physical access to it?
questions.explanation: Screen locks are explicitly listed as mobile-device hardening techniques.

questions.question: Which management approach is explicitly listed for mobile device security policies?
questions.explanation: MDM is explicitly listed under mobile security policies and procedures.

questions.lesson: 20B Troubleshoot Mobile OS and App Software
questions.question: An app repeatedly crashes immediately after launch. Which symptom category does this match?
options: Application fails to launch or crashes
questions.explanation: The mobile troubleshooting objectives explicitly include application fails to launch and application fails to close/crashes.

questions.lesson: 20B Troubleshoot Mobile OS and App Software
questions.question: Which connectivity technology is specifically listed for mobile troubleshooting?
questions.explanation: NFC is listed alongside Bluetooth and Wi-Fi as a mobile connectivity issue to troubleshoot.

questions.lesson: 20C Troubleshoot Mobile OS and App Security
questions.question: Which mobile-security symptom may indicate unauthorized or malicious application behavior?
questions.explanation: Unexpected application behavior is explicitly listed among common mobile security symptoms.

questions.lesson: 20C Troubleshoot Mobile OS and App Security
questions.question: Which mobile configuration increases security risk when it allows elevated access outside normal controls?
questions.explanation: Root access/jailbreak is explicitly identified as a mobile OS security concern.

questions.question: Which backup capability is specifically described for macOS?
questions.explanation: The Student Guide describes Time Machine as a macOS backup and recovery feature.

questions.question: When preparing to make a significant system change, which practice helps protect user data?
options: Perform or verify an appropriate backup
Delete the only copy of the data
questions.explanation: The support/troubleshooting material emphasizes checking backup status and performing a backup before changes when possible.

questions.question: Which method is specifically listed for physically destroying a hard drive?
questions.explanation: The security objectives list drilling, shredding, degaussing, and incineration as physical destruction methods.

questions.question: Which practice is associated with recycling or repurposing storage media?
questions.explanation: The objectives list erasing/wiping as a method under recycling or repurposing best practices.

questions.question: Which module contains Artificial Intelligence as an explicit lesson topic?
questions.explanation: The Student Guide contents identify Lesson 21C as Artificial Intelligence under Module 21.

questions.question: Which category does Artificial Intelligence appear under in the Core 2 Student Guide?
questions.explanation: The contents identify Module 21 as Using Data Security and Lesson 21C as Artificial Intelligence.

questions.question: Which change type is explicitly listed as requiring its own category in change management?
questions.explanation: The objectives list standard, normal, and emergency change types.

questions.question: Which document is used to define what happens if a change must be reversed?
questions.explanation: A rollback plan is explicitly listed as part of documented change-management processes.

questions.question: Which asset record can help verify whether hardware is still covered by support?
questions.explanation: The Student Guide states that procurement and warranty/support documentation should be recorded with asset information.

questions.question: Which practice reduces the risk of electrostatic discharge (ESD) when servicing sensitive components?
options: Use an appropriate antistatic wrist strap and ESD-safe work area
Store components loose on the desk
Work on a carpet without grounding
questions.explanation: The Student Guide describes ESD workstations, wrist straps, mats, and antistatic packaging as protective measures.

questions.question: Before replacing an internal PC component, what power-safety step is required?
options: Disconnect AC power and remove the battery if present
Insert tools into the power supply fan
questions.explanation: The Student Guide says to disconnect power first, remove the battery if present, and avoid opening power supplies because capacitors can retain dangerous charge.

questions.question: Which file extension is explicitly listed for a PowerShell script?
questions.explanation: .ps1 is listed among the script file types in the Core 2 objectives.

questions.question: Which is an example of a scripting use case listed in the objectives?
questions.explanation: The objectives list basic automation, restarting machines, remapping network drives, application installation, automated backups, gathering data, and initiating updates.

questions.question: Why should scripts be tested before deployment?
options: They can introduce malware, change system settings, or cause resource-related failures
Testing always makes scripts run slower
Testing is only required for hardware
questions.explanation: The objectives and Student Guide identify risks including malware introduction, unintended system-setting changes, and browser/system crashes from resource mishandling.

questions.question: A ticket describes an unexpected error affecting an end user. Which ticket type matches the Student Guide definition?
questions.explanation: An incident is an error or unexpected situation faced by an end user or customer.

questions.question: A help desk receives many incidents with the same underlying cause. Which ticket type is intended to represent the cause of incidents?
questions.explanation: A problem is the cause of incidents and may require analysis and service reconfiguration to solve.

questions.question: A technician needs to explain a technical issue to a nontechnical customer. Which communication approach is recommended?
options: Use plain language and avoid unnecessary jargon
Use as many technical acronyms as possible
Assume the customer already understands the terminology
Provide only command names without explanation
questions.explanation: The Student Guide emphasizes communication that customers can understand, including avoiding unnecessary technical jargon.

questions.question: Which filesystem is listed for Linux systems in the Core 2 objectives?
questions.explanation: ext4 is one of the filesystem types listed in the Core 2 objectives under common operating systems.

questions.question: A user wants Windows to show file extensions in File Explorer. Which setting category should the technician inspect?
questions.explanation: File Explorer Options contains settings controlling how files and folders are displayed, including hidden files and extensions.

questions.question: Which Windows feature is designed to request elevation when an action requires administrative privileges?
questions.explanation: UAC controls elevation prompts for administrative actions.

questions.question: An application requires a dedicated graphics card and a specified amount of video memory. Which installation consideration should be checked?
questions.explanation: Application system requirements can include graphics hardware, VRAM, RAM, CPU, storage, and OS compatibility.

questions.question: A company uses cloud storage and wants files synchronized between the service and a local folder. Which cloud-application setting is relevant?
questions.explanation: The Core 2 objectives specifically list sync/folder settings under cloud-based storage.

questions.question: A technician needs to manage scheduled automated tasks in Windows. Which MMC snap-in is appropriate?
questions.explanation: Task Scheduler (taskschd.msc) is the Windows management console for scheduled tasks.

questions.question: Which Windows console is used to manage hardware devices and their drivers?
questions.explanation: Device Manager (devmgmt.msc) manages devices and their drivers.

questions.question: Which command can display the Windows network configuration, including IP addressing information?
questions.explanation: ipconfig is used to display Windows IP configuration information.

questions.question: A Windows client is configured to receive its IP address automatically rather than having one manually assigned. Which addressing method is being used?
questions.explanation: Dynamic addressing means the address is obtained automatically; static addressing is manually assigned.

questions.question: A Windows workstation has network connectivity by IP address but cannot resolve hostnames. Which service configuration should be investigated?
questions.explanation: DNS provides name resolution, so DNS configuration should be checked when hostnames cannot be resolved.

questions.question: Which remote-access technology is Microsoft’s implementation of WS-Management?
questions.explanation: Windows Remote Management (WinRM) is Microsoft’s implementation of WS-Management.

questions.question: Which Windows tool is specifically used to monitor system performance counters and resource behavior?
questions.explanation: Performance Monitor (perfmon.msc) is the listed Windows tool for performance monitoring.

questions.question: A Windows system repeatedly displays a blue-screen error. Which troubleshooting category does this symptom belong to?
questions.explanation: A blue-screen error is listed as a common Windows operating-system problem.

questions.question: Which access model assumes access should not be trusted merely because a user is inside a network?
questions.explanation: The Core 2 objectives list the Zero Trust model as a logical security concept.

questions.question: Which technology provides centralized control of user identities, permissions, and access?
questions.explanation: IAM is listed as a logical security measure for managing identities and access.

questions.question: Which Windows encryption feature is specifically intended to protect files using the file system?
questions.explanation: EFS is the Windows feature listed for file-system-based encryption; BitLocker protects drives.

questions.question: When Windows shared resources are secured, which permission systems need to be considered together?
questions.explanation: The Core 2 objectives explicitly compare NTFS permissions with share permissions.

questions.question: Which Windows editions are explicitly listed for Windows 11 in the Core 2 objectives?
questions.explanation: The objectives list Windows 11 Home, Pro, and Enterprise.

questions.question: Which Windows feature is identified as an edition difference in the Core 2 objectives?
questions.explanation: RDP availability is listed as one of the feature differences between Windows editions.

questions.question: Which installation method is intended to repair an existing operating-system installation rather than perform a normal clean install?
questions.explanation: Repair installation is explicitly listed as an OS installation type.

questions.question: Which partitioning method is an alternative to Master Boot Record (MBR) in the objectives?
questions.explanation: GPT and MBR are the two partitioning schemes listed in the Core 2 objectives.

questions.question: Which command changes permissions on a Linux file or directory?
questions.explanation: chmod is the Linux command listed for changing file permissions.

questions.question: Which filesystem is listed for Linux and is distinct from ext4?
questions.explanation: XFS is another filesystem type listed in the Core 2 objectives for common operating systems.

questions.question: Which Linux command is used to manage software packages on Debian-family systems?
questions.explanation: apt is the package-management command listed for Debian-family Linux systems.

questions.question: Which macOS utility is specifically associated with managing disks and partitions?
questions.explanation: Disk Utility is the macOS utility used to manage disks and partitions.

questions.question: An attacker sends a deceptive message designed specifically for a high-profile executive. Which social-engineering attack is described?
questions.explanation: Whaling is a targeted phishing-style attack aimed at high-profile individuals such as executives.

questions.question: Which threat uses a fraudulent wireless access point that imitates a legitimate network?
questions.explanation: An evil twin is a fraudulent wireless access point designed to imitate a legitimate one.

questions.question: Which encryption standard is listed alongside TKIP under wireless security protocols?
questions.explanation: AES is listed with TKIP as a wireless security encryption technology.

questions.question: Which wireless network arrangement can provide visitors access without placing them on the main network?
questions.explanation: A guest network is used to provide separate access for visitors.

questions.question: Which account control limits how long a user can authenticate before the account expires?
questions.explanation: Account expiration dates are listed as an account-management hardening measure.

questions.question: Which Windows login option uses biometric information from the user's face?
questions.explanation: Facial recognition is one of the Windows login options listed in the objectives.

questions.question: Which password practice is explicitly included in workstation hardening?
questions.explanation: Password uniqueness is explicitly listed among workstation security considerations.

questions.question: A technician wants to reduce automatic execution from removable media. Which workstation setting is relevant?
questions.explanation: The objectives specifically list disabling AutoRun as a workstation hardening technique.

questions.question: Which mobile-security capability can remove organizational data from a lost device remotely?
questions.explanation: Remote wipes are explicitly listed as a mobile security measure.

questions.question: Which mobile management approach can enforce organizational device policies?
questions.explanation: MDM is listed for managing mobile device security policies and requirements.

questions.lesson: 20B Troubleshoot Mobile OS and App Software
questions.question: A mobile application works normally until a new version is installed, then it repeatedly crashes. Which troubleshooting area is directly involved?
questions.explanation: Repeated application crashes are a mobile OS and application software troubleshooting symptom.

questions.lesson: 20C Troubleshoot Mobile OS and App Security
questions.question: A device has been modified to allow elevated access outside the normal mobile OS security model. Which condition does this describe?
questions.explanation: Rooting or jailbreaking is the security-related mobile configuration that provides elevated access outside normal controls.

questions.question: Which backup strategy is specifically named in the Core 2 objectives?
questions.explanation: Grandfather-Father-Son (GFS) is explicitly listed among backup concepts in the objectives.

questions.question: Before performing a major system change, which action helps protect user data according to the operational guidance?
questions.explanation: Backing up and verifying data before significant changes is part of safe operational practice.

questions.question: Which data-destruction method uses a machine to physically reduce storage media to very small pieces?
questions.explanation: Shredding is listed as a physical data-destruction method.

questions.question: Where is Artificial Intelligence placed in the Core 2 Student Guide structure?
questions.explanation: Artificial Intelligence is an explicit topic in Module 21, Using Data Security.

questions.question: Which inventory record can help identify a device and link it to its lifecycle information?
questions.explanation: The Student Guide notes that a ticket may link device information to an inventory record through a service tag or asset ID.

questions.question: Which ESD-control practice is intended to safely discharge static electricity while servicing sensitive components?
options: Use an ESD wrist strap with an appropriate work area
Increase static charge before handling parts
questions.explanation: An ESD wrist strap and appropriate ESD-safe work area are listed practices for reducing electrostatic-discharge risk.
